subject: SOC 2 scope delta, log archival plan + capacity uplift (renewal cadence)
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acrosoft.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@acrosoft.com>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal question: SOC 2 scope delta + log retention

Hi Irene —

We're starting our renewal planning for July and I need to confirm a couple of things that affect our new policy:

1) SOC 2 scope delta: Our auditors want confirmation whether Redwood will include network-level forwarding logs in the attestation for the upcoming period. Previously the attestation covered application access logs only.

2) Log retention: We may need a longer retention window for audit trails (currently 90 days). Can you confirm if 12-month retention is supported for the log collection we send (and whether it triggers any pricing/ingress changes)?

3) Capacity uplift: If we increase seat/throughput commitments to match projected usage, can we get the SOC 2 recertification bundled into the renewal and a 30% credit on incremental committed spend during the first 6 months?

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can align procurement with the audit timeline.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Security, Acrosoft
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acrosoft.com>
Cc: James Liu <james.liu@acrosoft.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question: SOC 2 scope delta + log retention

Hi Ellen —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. Looping in our Security lead Marissa and Compliance ops (Jonas) to confirm the technical/contract implications. High-level answers below and next steps:

- SOC 2 scope delta: We can accommodate network-level forwarding logs in the attestation, but this is considered a scope change (adds evidence buckets + control mapping). We need to run a short impact assessment (3–4 business days) to map the controls and identify any evidence gaps.

- Log retention: 12-month retention is supported for audit archives. There are two paths:
  * Managed retention (Redwood hosts the archive): small monthly uplift based on ingested GB and retention tier.
  * Customer-hosted archive (push to your S3/GCS): no retention charge from us, but requires an integration step and verification for evidence collection.

- Capacity uplift + pricing: We can bundle the SOC 2 scope change into the renewal with a one-time SOC engineering fee and apply a promotional commit credit for incremental capacity. I'll outline options in a formal offer.

Next steps (action owners):
  1) Marissa to run scope impact assessment and list required evidence artifacts (ETA: 3 business days) — marissa.cole@redwood.ai
  2) Jonas to estimate log-storage uplift and propose pricing for managed retention (ETA: 2 business days) — jonas.weber@redwood.ai
  3) Irene to draft renewal amendment options (terms + commit credit) and share draft redline (ETA: EOD Tue 05/23) — irene.choi@redwood.ai

I'll keep James and your procurement team updated. If that timeline works, we'll attach the evidence checklist and a proposed amendment for review.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, Ellen Park <ellen.park@acrosoft.com>

Date: Mon, 21 May 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal question: SOC 2 scope delta + log retention

Hi all —

I've completed the scope impact assessment and attached a checklist (soc2_scope_delta_checklist.xlsx). Key notes:

- Network forwarding logs can be included, but we need the following artifacts from Acrosoft for mapping:
  * Sample forwarding configuration and schema
  * Expected volume (avg/day) and peak window
  * Any filtered fields that are redacted prior to forwarding

- Evidence implications: We will need additional controls mapped under CC6, CC7 for monitoring/retention and a new procedure for verifying integrity of archived logs.

- Evidence collection approach: We recommend Redwood-managed archival for the first cycle so our auditors can pull evidence directly (simpler for attestation). If you prefer S3 push, we'll need an access profile and verification run.

I've also prepared a log_retention_matrix.csv showing cost bands at 90/180/365-day tiers. Jonas, happy to sync on estimated bill impact.

Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: soc2_scope_delta_checklist.xlsx

Ellen —

Attached is the quick cost summary and two optional offers: Managed Archive (Redwood-hosted) and Push-to-S3. Summary:

- Managed Archive (365 days): ~+12% on monthly FYR bill for storage + small engineering onboarding fee (one-time).
- Push-to-S3: no ongoing Redwood storage charge but we require a one-time verification and an automated snapshot job (small one-time engineering fee).

On the capacity uplift/commit credit: we can offer a structured commit that gives a 25% credit on incremental compute for the first 90 days and a 15% credit for the following 3 months, provided the uplift is committed in the contract amendment. We can push the promotional credit to 30% if the commit is 12 months and includes a minimal seat increase of 20%.

I've added procurement-friendly language to the renewal_terms_redline_v2.docx and added a HubSpot deal note under ACRO123.

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

2) 365-day retention for archived logs (managed).
3) We'll take the 12-month commit (20% uplift) to qualify for the 30% incremental compute credit for months 1–6.
